Set back across the water and above, the large multi-storey inn stacks up the slope behind the bath, turned three-quarters so one long wing recedes left into shadow; dark timber and white plaster rise across five stepped levels; warm amber rectangles glow across every storey; its eave boards plain dark timber, smooth and unmarked; the hanging noren at the doorway carrying one painted pine sprig and no other marking.

Off to one side and set back, a single low cedar bath-house presents one enormous overhanging eave, seen obliquely so its shallow body falls away rightward; white plaster panels sit between dark posts; a grid of soft paper-screen glow runs the near face; its round lanterns plain warm cream, each face a single unbroken wash of colour; the upright plank by the entrance painted over with a single grey wave-crest motif.

Behind and above, a long wing with a wraparound balcony faces us at three-quarters so its far end recedes into the slope; deep shingled eaves cap two storeys of dark timber and plaster; one upstairs screen burns brighter than the three others beside it; the hanging cloth at the doorway one flat colour end to end; the doorway plank bearing one painted maple leaf, the rest bare cedar.

Close on the near side, a covered walkway on posts leads back from the bath's edge toward the inn, seen obliquely so its row of nine posts diminishes into the building's flank; lantern brackets hang at every third post; paper screens behind the near posts glow with soft amber; a smooth bare cedar plank beside the doorway carries one painted crane and nothing more; the noren beside the doorway painted with a single white crane in outline.

Behind and slightly raised, a small changing shed with a deep overhang stands turned three-quarters so its narrow gable end faces us and its long side falls away; dark timber frame, white plaster infill, a single deep eave of rough cedar shingle; one wide paper screen glows warm from within; its short entry curtain a plain deep indigo with one small painted pine sprig and nothing else; the round paper lantern at the threshold carrying one painted circle of indigo and nothing more.

Set back across the water, a half-roofed shelter reaches over one end of the bath on heavy cedar posts, seen obliquely so its ridge line angles away; rough-sawn timber, an open side facing the water, three paper lanterns of odd count strung along the inner beam; the nearer two glow evenly and one outer lantern glows a shade brighter; its eave boards plain dark timber, smooth and unmarked; the hanging noren at the doorway carrying one painted pine sprig and no other marking.

Off to one side at middle distance, a cluster of five separate little cabins with lit screens steps up a gentle rise, seen obliquely so each cabin stands slightly behind and overlapping the next; dark timber frames, low shingled roofs; every cabin shows a single warm amber rectangle of paper screen; its round lanterns plain warm cream, each face a single unbroken wash of colour; the upright plank by the entrance painted over with a single grey wave-crest motif.

Behind and above, an old main hall with a steep shingled roof dominates the frame, turned three-quarters so its broad ridge runs back into the hillside; dark heavy timber and pale plaster, deep tiled eaves casting shadow below; a row of seven paper screens glows across the upper storey and one leftmost screen stands part-open showing a brighter gap; its round lanterns plain warm cream, each face a single unbroken wash of colour; the doorway plank bearing one painted maple leaf, the rest bare cedar.

Stacked up the slope behind the bath, a tall narrow inn with lit balconies on three floors is seen obliquely so its short width faces us and its depth vanishes uphill; dark timber rail caps each balcony; warm paper screens glow at every level; the hanging cloth at the doorway one flat colour end to end; the noren beside the doorway painted with a single white crane in outline.

A modest family inn with one warm window and a lit doorway sits close on the near side, turned three-quarters so one low eave reaches toward us and the rear wall falls away; rough plaster between dark posts, a single paper screen alight upstairs and a warm glow at the open entry below; its short entry curtain a plain deep indigo with one small painted moon and nothing else; the round paper lantern at the threshold carrying one painted circle of indigo and nothing more.

Behind and above, the large multi-storey inn is seen now from a steeper angle, one broad gabled face toward us and the far stepped wing receding right; white plaster panels catch the warmth from within; five paper screens glow across the middle storey, the central one burning softer than the two on each side; a smooth bare cedar plank beside the doorway carries one painted wave and nothing more; the hanging noren at the doorway carrying one painted pine sprig and no other marking.

Off to one side, a covered walkway on posts angles away from the near bath edge, seen obliquely so its lean-to roof diminishes in perspective; cedar posts dark with age; three lanterns hang at uneven intervals along the beam, the far one slightly higher than the nearer pair; their faces plain warm cream, each a single unbroken wash of colour; its eave boards plain dark timber, smooth and unmarked; the upright plank by the entrance painted over with a single grey wave-crest motif.

Set back across the water, a long two-storey wing with a wraparound balcony is turned three-quarters so its corner post stands near and its far rail vanishes left; dark timber balustrade, white plaster above and below; a grid of amber paper-screen rectangles runs the full upper storey; the hanging cloth at the doorway one flat colour end to end; the doorway plank bearing one painted maple leaf, the rest bare cedar.

Close on the near side with its eave reaching out, a small bath-house shows a single enormous shingled overhang, seen obliquely so the peak angles away and the far eave drops into shadow; one wide paper screen glows softly from inside; its eave boards plain dark timber, smooth and unmarked; the noren beside the doorway painted with a single white crane in outline.

Stacked up the slope behind and above, the old main hall is now seen obliquely from the other quarter, its long south face falling away and the steep shingled gable cutting the upper frame; dark timber exposed at the corners; nine paper screens along the lower gallery glow in amber, the third from left brighter and standing part-open; its short entry curtain a plain deep indigo with one small painted mountain outline and nothing else; the round paper lantern at the threshold carrying one painted circle of indigo and nothing more.

Behind and raised, a half-roofed shelter on cedar posts extends over the far edge, turned three-quarters so its open flank faces us and its closed rear wall recedes; rough-hewn beams overhead, three paper lanterns of odd count along the inner ridge; the outermost lantern hangs a fraction lower; each lantern face a single unbroken wash of plain warm cream; the hanging noren at the doorway carrying one painted pine sprig and no other marking.

Off to one side at the mid-distance, a cluster of three small cabins with lit screens sits turned so the nearest cabin shows its short gable and the two behind diminish in a diagonal; dark shingle roofs, white plaster walls, each cabin showing one soft amber rectangle; a smooth bare cedar plank beside the nearest doorway carries one painted spiral and nothing more; the upright plank by the entrance painted over with a single grey wave-crest motif.

Behind the bath on a level terrace, a modest family inn faces three-quarters right so one low wing falls away; a single room glows upstairs and the open entry below spills a soft amber patch onto the terrace plank; dark timber and worn plaster; its eave boards plain dark timber, smooth and unmarked; the doorway plank bearing one painted maple leaf, the rest bare cedar.

Set back at the far end, a tall narrow inn is seen obliquely so its three balconies on three floors stack into perspective; dark timber rails and white plaster piers; warm paper screens fill each floor, the topmost screen brighter than the five below; a smooth bare cedar plank beside the ground-floor step carries one painted pine sprig and nothing more; the noren beside the doorway painted with a single white crane in outline.

Close on the near side, a changing shed with a deep overhang is turned so its short gable end faces directly and the long low body recedes into shadow behind it; dark cedar posts frame a single glowing paper screen; its short entry curtain a plain deep indigo with one small painted leaf and nothing else; the round paper lantern at the threshold carrying one painted circle of indigo and nothing more.

Behind and above, the large stacked inn is turned three-quarters on, the stepped roofline rising left to right; dark tiled eaves overhang deep between floors; seven paper screens glow across the second storey, one right-of-centre standing part-open and showing a brighter gap; its round lanterns plain warm cream, each face a single unbroken wash of colour; the hanging noren at the doorway carrying one painted pine sprig and no other marking.

Off to one side, the covered walkway on posts is now seen from behind so the posts march toward the bath, diminishing in odd perspective; a cedar lean-to roof slopes above; five lanterns hang along the beam, the first and middle and last slightly brighter; a smooth bare cedar plank beside the near post carries one painted pine sprig and nothing more; the upright plank by the entrance painted over with a single grey wave-crest motif.

Stacked up the slope, the two-storey wing with a wraparound balcony is turned now so its far end faces us and its long rail recedes right; white plaster and dark timber, deep shingled eaves; a row of paper screens glows along the near face, the leftmost screen burning warmer than the three beside it; the hanging cloth at the doorway one flat colour end to end; the doorway plank bearing one painted maple leaf, the rest bare cedar.

Set back across the water, the single low cedar bath-house is seen at a new angle, its enormous eave now in profile slanting across the upper frame; white plaster glows faintly between dark posts; three paper screens of unequal brightness run the near wall, the centre one fullest; its eave boards plain dark timber, smooth and unmarked; the noren beside the doorway painted with a single white crane in outline.

Behind and above at the top of the slope, a small changing shed stands isolated, turned three-quarters so its narrow face presents to us and its body falls away into the dark hillside; one amber paper screen glows in the near wall; its short entry curtain a plain deep indigo with one small painted circle and nothing else; the round paper lantern at the threshold carrying one painted circle of indigo and nothing more.
